A timestep $t$ and a layer $l$ are sampled. An ordered sequence $ _ $ of $b$ channels is drawn without replacement by Gumbel top-$b$, giving the mask $m_K$. The frozen diffusion model $D$ returns $G_{t,l}(x)$ after the alignment $A_l$, and masking gives $ F_a(x)$. This feature is the distillation target for the student $S_ $ and, through the task decoder $q_ $, gives the reward $R=- _{ {dec}}$. The policy is updated by REINFORCE with baseline $c$ and the channel score scaled by $1/b$ (Equation~ {eq:balanced}). At inference, only $S_ $ is evaluated. Images and predictions are ADE20K validation examples (Figure~ {fig:qualitative}).

page_papers.title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions
page_papers.abstract: This paper shows that JEPA-style latent world models (LWMs) can learn across diverse domains and data sources by adopting the language-conditioned interface of video generation models. We establish this approach as an effective and efficient basis for planning with imagination and downstream policy fine-tuning. To this end, we introduce LaLa-World, a Language-conditioned Latent World model that learns from simulation and robot trajectories together with broader image and video data. Two designs make this work. First, we describe both numerical actions and visual changes in language, enabling joint training of a single future predictor across heterogeneous datasets. Second, we build the predictor on a language model, allowing it to interpret language conditions while predicting future latent states. The resulting predictor achieves higher average MPC planning performance than existing LWMs trained separately for each domain or task. Adding image and video data further improves average planning performance and robustness to action phrasing. In a matched comparison with an RAEv2-based video generation model baseline, LaLa-World reaches comparable planning performance with 6times less training cost and 13.9times faster planning. Beyond planning, the pretrained LaLa-World serves as an initialization for LaLa-Policy, which jointly predicts actions and future visual representations. LaLa-Policy performs competitively with Cosmos Policy on LIBERO and RoboCasa, with up to 5.5times faster inference.

Introduction
A central capability of an intelligent agent is to anticipate how the world will change in response to its actions.
Before pushing a cup across a table, we know where it will end up and whether it might fall.
World models capture this capability by predicting future states under candidate actions, providing a basis for planning or decision-making
(
Sutton, 1991
;
Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018
;
LeCun, 2022
;
Hafner et al., 2020
)
.
A promising approach to making this predictive capability computationally efficient is to model how visual representations change under actions, without learning to reconstruct images at the pixel level.
This motivates our focus on JEPA-style latent world models (LWMs), such as V-JEPA 2-AC
(
Assran et al., 2025
)
and DINO-WM
(
Zhou et al., 2025
)
.

This efficiency of LWMs is particularly useful for planning with imagination in the latent space, which requires repeatedly evaluating candidate action sequences, by rolling out multiple candidate futures at low cost

However, despite this advantage, the action-conditioned predictors in such LWMs have largely been trained on simulation or robotics datasets, where numerical actions have domain-specific dimensions and physical meanings.
For example,

Furthermore, image and video data, which provide a rich source of observations of the world, often lack these numerical action annotations, making them difficult to use for training action-conditioned future predictors.
Therefore, scaling LWMs across diverse control actions and broader image and video data requires a shared interface that accommodates heterogeneous data.
We suggest that language can serve as the shared interface.
We introduce LaLa-World, a language-conditioned LWM that learns from diverse control datasets and broader image and video data with a single future predictor.
Language conditioning already supports learning from diverse visual data in video generation

Conclusion
We presented LaLa-World, a latent world model that learns from heterogeneous control trajectories and broader image and video data through a shared language interface.
This enables comparisons with existing LWMs in MPC planning and generative models in planning and policy fine-tuning.
Despite sharing one predictor across domains, LaLa-World outperforms existing LWMs in average MPC planning performance.
Under matched settings, including training data, it also surpasses the generative baseline in planning performance and efficiency.
Following Cosmos Policy’s use of world models pretrained on diverse data for policy learning, we fine-tuned LaLa-World into LaLa-Policy.
It outperforms evaluated VLA baselines and achieves substantially faster inference than Cosmos Policy.
These results demonstrate the value of latent world models for planning and policy learning without training to reconstruct visual details.
We hope this work draws greater attention to latent world models, their scalability, and downstream uses.
For broader practical impact, future work could explore scaling training data and model size, extending prediction horizons, and evaluating policies on real robots, as discussed in

article.headline: 语言作动作接口，潜空间世界模型可跨域规划
article.lede: LaLa-World 用自然语言统一动作接口，让 JEPA 式潜空间世界模型能同时吃下控制轨迹与视频数据。
article.problem: 现有 JEPA 式潜空间世界模型（如 V-JEPA 2-AC、DINO-WM）的动作条件预测器基本只在仿真或机器人数据上训练，而数值动作的维度和物理含义随域变化——同一个 [2,4] 在一个域里是水平/垂直位移，在另一个域里含义完全不同，难以学到共享动力学。同时，图像与视频数据量大却普遍缺少数值动作标注，无法直接用于训练动作条件预测器。因此要把这类模型规模化到多域、多源数据，需要一个能容纳异构数据的共享接口。
article.method: 作者提出用自然语言作为共享接口：把数值动作和视觉变化都描述成语言条件，从而用同一个预测器在控制数据与更广的图像视频数据上联合训练。模型以语言模型为骨干，输入编码后的观测与语言条件，预测未来的视觉表征，不重建像素。在规划阶段用 MPC + CEM 在潜空间里滚动候选动作序列并选出最接近目标的一条；再把预训练的 LaLa-World 微调成 LaLa-Policy，同时输出动作块和对应的未来潜表征。
article.results: 论文报告，尽管所有域共享同一个预测器，LaLa-World 在仿真与机器人两组基准上的平均 MPC 规划得分均为最高（材料中未给出具体数值）。在 RoboCasa 上，LaLa-Policy 与改造后的 Cosmos Policy 基线表现相当，同时每条轨迹的平均推理时间减少 5.5 倍。ImageNet 变换预测实验中，材料仅保留了 IWM 基线的 MRR 0.79（默认设置）与 0.85（强抖动），LaLa-World 自身的 MRR 数值未在材料中给出。策略微调方面，从 LaLa-World 初始化在 LIBERO 与 RoboCasa 上均优于随机初始化与 Qwen3.5 初始化，但材料未给出具体数字。
article.why_it_matters: 它提示了一条不依赖像素重建的世界模型扩展路径：语言接口把不同维度、不同物理含义的动作和没有动作标注的视频统一起来，同一个预测器即可跨域规划，并可作为策略微调的有效初始化。
article.limitations: 所有策略与规划实验都在 LIBERO、RoboCasa 等仿真环境完成，尚未在真实机器人上验证；作者也承认，通过语言接口做 LLM 规划仅在较小的想象预算下可行，在需要精细控制的任务上仍有明显提升空间。此外材料中关键数值（规划得分、策略成功率、消融结果）缺失，无法独立判断提升幅度。
article.figure_caption_zh: 用 MPC 在潜空间中想象候选语言动作下的未来表征并挑选通向目标的最优动作，同一预测器可跨域规划，底部两行展示无数值的纯语言动作。
